input.quote: A. Customer acknowledges and agrees that the Monthly Base Fee pricing offered to Customer by M&I is based on certain services provided by M&I's Integrated Banking System. Customer agrees that, during the Term, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee, as set forth on Schedule 6.2.
input.rationale: Section 8.1(ii) imposes a "minimum monthly fee ("Monthly Base Fee")" and Section 10.3(A) requires us to take the entire bundled set of Services from M&I for the whole Term (to the eighth anniversary of the Effective Date), with the minimum feeding the Estimated Remaining Value termination-fee formula in p0039. There is no right to reduce volumes or drop Services, while M&I may withdraw non-Core Services on 90 days' notice under 10.2. That is a multi-year take-or-pay that fails the fallback. Eliminating the Monthly Base Fee entirely (preferred) would unwind the bundled pricing bargain, so we take the fallback: the commitment runs only through the then-current twelve (12) month period and is reducible on 30 days' notice with an equitable true-up of the Monthly Base Fee instead of a shortfall penalty.

ops.oldText: Customer agrees that, during the Term, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee
ops.newText: Customer agrees that, during the then-current twelve (12) month period, Customer shall be required to obtain from M&I all of those Services which are included in the Monthly Base Fee

ops.text: Customer may, upon 30 days' notice to M&I, reduce or discontinue any Service included in the Monthly Base Fee, in which case the Monthly Base Fee shall be equitably reduced to reflect the resource units no longer used, as a true-up rather than a shortfall penalty.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We changed the commitment period from the full eight-year Term to the then-current twelve (12) month period and added a right to reduce or discontinue bundled Services on 30 days' notice with an equitable true-up of the Monthly Base Fee rather than a shortfall penalty, consistent with our minimum-commitment fallback.
proposal.summary: Limit the Monthly Base Fee bundle commitment to the then-current 12-month period and make it reducible on 30 days' notice with a true-up

mappings.element: Commitment limited to the current 12-month term.
